blocks.content: Freedom came with the immense responsibility of building a united, democratic, and prosperous nation out of vast diversity.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Independent India faced three main initial challenges: maintaining unity amid diversity, sustaining a democratic political order, and ensuring equitable economic development.
The partition of 1947 triggered widespread communal violence, massive displacement, and urgent refugee rehabilitation issues.
The integration of over 560 princely states required diplomatic negotiation and firm leadership to consolidate national territory.
Reorganizing states on a linguistic basis proved crucial in accommodating regional aspirations while strengthening national unity.
Frequently tested: The role of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and the Instrument of Accession in integrating princely states.
Important for prelims: The recommendations of the States Reorganisation Commission (1953) and the States Reorganisation Act of 1956.
Key concept: The initial three-fold post-independence challenges (Unity, Democracy, Development).
